plan.title: Whole blood case vs control DE + effect-size triage + pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: 60 cases vs 60 controls, whole-blood bulk RNA-seq, raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 121 columns incl. gene symbol, 120 samples), single batch, unpaired. At n=60/group the count-based negative-binomial models (DESeq2/edgeR) are documented to inflate false positives on population cohorts because sample-to-sample variance departs from the NB assumption even under permuted labels; the grounded procedure for this regime is limma-voom with TMM normalization and a fixed-effects linear model, cross-checked against a non-parametric Wilcoxon rank-sum test as a robustness control. Because large n gives the test power to call biologically trivial effects significant, the plan explicitly separates 'differs' (BH-adjusted p<0.05) from 'differs enough to matter' by requiring TREAT-style testing against a stated log2FC threshold and reporting apeglm-shrunken effect sizes and CIs alongside p-values, sorted by effect size rather than p-value alone. Pathway-level structure follows with camera (accounts for inter-gene correlation, appropriate for the large-n fixed design) and fgsea-preranked on the moderated-t statistic against MSigDB Hallmark and Reactome, since a handful of coordinated small-effect genes below the single-gene significance list may still mark a pathway. All choices, thresholds, and reference collection versions are recorded in the report for reproducibility.

apeglm (via DESeq2 for effect-size reporting alongside limma-voom test)
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, TREAT threshold test against lfc
camera on limma fit (Hallmark), fgsea preranked on moderated t (Hallmark + Reactome)
integrated report with effect sizes, diagnostics, reproducibility record

limma-voom fixed-effects linear model with Wilcoxon rank-sum control
